The appearance of rheumatoid factor (RF) may precede 
symptoms of RA. Pain, stiffness, swelling, loss of function, and 
anemia are common. The swelling or puffiness is caused by the 
accumulation of synovial fluid in the membrane lining the joints 
and inflammation of the surrounding tissues (see Figure 39-4).
Some controversy exists regarding green tea: it has been sug-
gested that drinking large amounts of tea may increase the risk 
of developing RA, whereas other studies suggest a protective 
role (Walitt et al, 2010; Wu et al, 2012). Smoking is the environ-
mental risk factor that is most associated with RA followed by 
coffee consumption, whereas dietary antioxidants and breast-
feeding may be protective (Lahiri et al, 2012).
